parsed.headline: Yemen military holds mass funeral for 75 recruits killed in Houthi missile strike

pages.text: Yemen's military held a mass funeral on Wednesday for 75 new recruits killed during a Houthi missile strike in south-central Shabwa province. According to reporting by Africanews, the strike occurred on October 19, 2026, at the al-Alam camp while the recruits, aged between 18 and 20, were lining up in formation for a training session. The governor of Shabwa stated the recruits were being trained to provide security in the province rather than for combat operations. In addition to the fatalities, 200 others were wounded in the attack. The funeral ceremony was held in a soccer field at the site of the strike and was attended by senior government and military officials as troops and security forces carried the coffins of the deceased. Following the ceremony, the governor of Shabwa pledged to increase efforts to defend the province and vowed to pursue those responsible for the strike to hold them accountable.

parsed.headline: Druze population in Golan Heights shows increased interest in Israeli citizenship following 2025 military strikes in Syria

pages.text: According to interior ministry figures reported by Arab News, approximately 45 percent of the 26,000 Druze living in the Golan Heights held Israeli nationality as of October 21, 2026, compared to 2 percent forty years ago. This shift in attitude follows military strikes carried out by Israel in Syria in 2025. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the attacks were intended to protect Syria’s Druze population. Some residents interviewed by AFP identified Israel's 2025 intervention in Syria’s Sweida province, which is predominantly Druze, as a turning point in their perspective. In Majdal Shams, a Golan Druze city of 12,000 people, citizenship applications rose to 3,750 in 2025 from 570 the previous year. Historically, the Golan's Druze have rejected outward allegiance to Israel, which captured the territory from Syria in 1967 and annexed it in 1981. Political expert Salim Brik noted that because nearly all Druze in the territory have family in Syria, there was an initial social and religious boycott of Israel. While the annexation has been recognized by the United States and Colombia, the Druze population in the Golan has historically differed from other Arabic-speaking groups in Israel who are integrated and required to serve in the military.

parsed.headline: Oshawa voter turnout was 18.4 per cent in 2022 ahead of 2026 municipal election

pages.text: In the 2022 municipal election in Oshawa, Canada, 18.4 per cent of eligible residents cast a ballot. This turnout was lower than the average for the Durham Region during the same election, which was just under 24 per cent. The upcoming municipal election is scheduled for October 19, 2026, and will feature nine candidates seeking to replace outgoing Mayor Dan Carter. For the first time this year, Oshawa residents will have the option to vote online. To participate, voters must be on the voters' list. Unregistered residents can visit the voter assistance centre at Oshawa City Hall, located at 50 Centre Street S., to be added to the list. The centre is open from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily until October 16, 2026.

parsed.headline: US embassy accuses Canada of election interference ahead of midterms

pages.text: In a fact sheet released on October 21, 2026, the United States embassy accused Canadian politicians of attempting to influence the upcoming November 3 midterm elections. According to Al Jazeera, the US embassy alleged that the Canadian government has been dismissive of these concerns, claiming that ministers and premiers have described plans to influence American politics in public appearances and official documents. The allegations follow a trade war between the two nations that began at the start of President Donald Trump’s second term in 2025, characterized by US tariffs and reciprocal Canadian import taxes. The US embassy identified public statements regarding these tariffs as attempts to sway the midterm election, citing Canadian tariffs, political meetings, and anti-Trump advertisements as evidence of interference.

The US embassy singled out Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly in the fact sheet, pointing to comments she made in August regarding the response to US tariffs. Joly stated at the time, “We’re also targeting products that will target states in the US. And so we’re being wise and strategic to put political pressure.” The embassy also cited Joly’s September meetings with Democratic officials in Boston and Chicago. When asked by a reporter about potential tariff outcomes if Democrats won the midterms, Joly responded, “That’s exactly why I’m meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates.” Joly has rejected the suggestion that her actions constitute interference, stating that Canada would never meddle in US elections.

parsed.headline: MobileMoney Fintech LTD signs partnership to expand digital finance for MSMEs in Ghana

pages.text: MobileMoney Fintech LTD has signed a strategic partnership with the United Nations Capital Development Fund and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development to expand digital financial services for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Ghana. The agreement was signed in Accra by Shaibu Haruna, Chief Executive Officer of MobileMoney Fintech LTD, and Allen Anie, Head of Experimentation and Chief Technical Adviser at UNDP, who initialled for the UN system. The signing was witnessed by officials from the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry and senior management from MobileMoney Fintech LTD. Under the Joint SDG Fund programme, the partnership aims to leverage digital ecosystems to increase MSME productivity and advance financial inclusion. Shaibu Haruna stated that the programme focuses on underserved groups, specifically women and youth-led businesses, and intends to address financial health pillars including savings, micro-loans, and group loans.

parsed.headline: Inflation estimated to have pushed 8 to 10 million people below poverty line in Bangladesh

pages.text: Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, the Prime Minister’s Adviser on Finance and Planning in Bangladesh, stated that inflation has placed a heavy burden on low- and middle-income citizens, resulting in an estimated 8 million to 10 million people falling below the poverty line. Titumir made these remarks to journalists on a Wednesday afternoon during a meeting organized by the Rajbari District Administration at the Rajbari Municipality auditorium. Rajbari District Council Administrator Abdus Salam Mia was also in attendance. 1. Titumir cited a World Bank report and noted that the introduction of farmer and family cards has been recognized by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank as an initiative intended to reduce poverty and ease hardship. 2. Describing the current economic state as a fragile transition, Titumir said the administration inherited high inflation, rising unemployment, and weak private-sector investment. He noted that rising prices have forced many individuals to use savings or take on debt, and highlighted unemployment among young, educated citizens as a major concern. 3. Titumir attributed increased pressure on the economy to rising fuel prices caused by the Middle East crisis and alleged that the previous government failed to expand solar energy, explore domestic gas, or ensure sustainable energy security. He further alleged that cronyism and patronage weakened the economic system, stating that approximately US$40 billion is now required to repair the banking sector. 4. To address these issues, Titumir emphasized the need to develop renewable energy to reduce dependence on imported fuel, reform the education system, and develop a skilled workforce to combat unemployment.

parsed.headline: First nationwide count finds over 1 million mice and 46,000 rats used in Australian research annually

pages.text: A pilot study conducted for the Australian and New Zealand Council for the Care of Animals in Research and Teaching has reported that 1,193,619 mice and 46,961 rats were used for scientific research, teaching, and testing in Australia in 2024. The figure represents the first nationwide count of its kind, though it does not include animals bred for research purposes that were not used. The study focused on mice and rats because they are widely used in biomedical research. According to veterinarian Dr. Malcolm France, who compiled the data, the count is an overdue step toward publishing national statistics for all research animals, including birds, monkeys, fish, and rabbits. Dr. France noted that while New South Wales, Victoria, and Tasmania consistently publish animal use data, other jurisdictions either collect statistics without sharing them or do not collect them at all. Establishing the national figure required various methods, including a freedom of information request. Dr. France stated that national statistics are used in the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, the European Union, and New Zealand to inform resource allocation and animal welfare priorities. Bella Lear, chief executive of Understanding Animal Research Oceania, said nationwide data is vital for demonstrating the scope of Australian research and its animal welfare practices.

parsed.headline: Journalist Sohrab Hossain laid to rest in Patuakhali, Bangladesh

pages.text: Md Sohrab Hossain, a correspondent for The Daily Star in Patuakhali for over 22 years and vice-president of the Patuakhali Press Club, was laid to rest on the morning of October 21, 2026, at his family graveyard in Auliapur, Patuakhali. His namaz-e-janaza was held at 10:00am at the Auliapur Sabina Akter High School grounds, attended by local residents, colleagues, fellow journalists, and relatives. During the service, his sons, Atikur Rahman and Sufian Molla, spoke. Representatives from various social, political, and professional organizations, including The Daily Star’s Content Editor Md Al-Amin and Patuakhali Press Club President Zakir Hossain, also paid their respects. Following the ceremony, Hossain was buried next to the grave of his elder brother, Maulana Wahab Molla. According to The Daily Star, Hossain joined the publication on January 1, 2004.

Hossain died at Patuakhali Medical College Hospital on October 20, 2026, at the age of 55. A hospital death certificate listed cardiac arrest as the cause of death. Family members stated that on the morning of October 21, 2026, Hossain was riding a motorbike from his village home in Auliapur toward his residence at Banani Mor. At approximately 8:30am, he reportedly felt pain and stopped near the Molla bus stand before collapsing on the road. Local residents and family members transported him to the hospital, where he later died.
